I built this because I got sick of re-pairing my Magic Keyboard and Mouse every time I moved between my MacBook and my work MacBook — different Apple IDs, so Universal Control was never going to work for me. LinkFlick just flicks them over Bluetooth instead. Hotkey, or tell Siri "flick devices," done. Menu bar app, customizable hotkey, and it nags you before your Magic Mouse battery dies. Still rough around the edges in places, but it works, and it's mine.

results.title: Thirty windows, one button - Product Hunt
results.content:
Captain Kill Switch is one button in your menu bar that closes every running app. Simon Crean built it after the same stupid moment kept repeating, finishing for the day with thirty-odd windows open and shutting them one at a time, which he describes as tidying a room by picking up individual grains of rice. No dashboard, no settings, no account. Anything still open a couple of seconds later gets force-closed, unsaved work and all, and he says that on the launch page rather than letting you find out on a Friday evening, which is the right way round.

LinkFlick — Stop re-pairing your Magic Keyboard between Macs [...] LinkFlick throws your Magic Keyboard and mouse from one Mac to the other on a hotkey. Roman Abramenko has a personal MacBook and a work MacBook sitting six inches apart on two different Apple IDs, which is exactly the arrangement Universal Control refuses to accept exists. So the Bluetooth handover happens on a keystroke instead of in System Settings. His own summary is that it is not fancy and does one job, and the thing he actually asks for in the comments is people telling him where it breaks on their setup.
